title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Assignment data (work file, student ID, course, timestamp) transmitted from Student to Grades Portal Web App could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transit, potentially exposing sensitive academic information.

title: Linkability via Metadata
description: Metadata accompanying the assignment submission (student ID, course, timestamp) could be used to link this data with other records, potentially enabling profiling or correlation attacks.

title: Excessive Data Collection at Destination
description: Grades Portal Web App may collect and store more data than necessary for the assignment submission purpose, including potentially sensitive student identifiers beyond what's required for grading.

title: Student Identification at Destination
description: The system processes and stores student identification data (student ID) which could be used to identify the student across multiple contexts or systems.

title: Identity Usurpation Risk at Source
description: Student's login credentials and identity information could be compromised during the authentication process, allowing unauthorized access to the submission system.

title: Identifier exposure in transit
description: The data flow transmits student id, course, file reference, and requesting role - all containing unique references to the student's identity. This identifier data is exposed during transit between P1 and P2, creating a risk of unauthorized identification.
assumptions: Data is transmitted without adequate encryption or access controls
uncertainty_note: Using I.2.1.1 from context as it directly matches the identifier nature of the data

title: Processing of identified data at destination
description: The Assignment & Grading Service (P2) receives and processes identified data (student id, course, file reference). This processing of personally identifiable information creates privacy risks if the service lacks appropriate safeguards or if the data is retained longer than necessary.
assumptions: P2 processes the data for grading purposes
uncertainty_note: I.1.1 from context applies to processing of identified data

title: Linkability of student submissions
description: The combination of student id, course, and file reference in the data flow enables linking of the student to their specific submissions and grades. This creates a persistent link between the student's identity and their academic activities.
assumptions: The identifiers are combined and can be correlated
uncertainty_note: Using I.2.1.1 as it covers the identifier-based linking aspect

title: Processing of identified teacher-submission data
description: The Grades Portal Web App processes identified data (teacher identity linked to submission queue), which could expose personal information about teachers and their grading activities.

title: Linkability of teacher identity to submissions
description: Metadata in the data flow could link teacher identity to specific submissions, potentially revealing which teacher reviewed which student work.

title: Usurpation of teacher identity during authentication
description: Teacher's login credentials could be compromised, allowing unauthorized access to submission queues and impersonation of the teacher.

title: Linkability of student identities through submission data in transit
description: Student names and work content transmitted in the data flow could be linked to identify individual students, potentially enabling unauthorized correlation of student identities with their submissions.

title: Identification of students through direct name sharing
description: The Grades Portal Web App shares student names with the teacher, directly identifying students and enabling the teacher to link submissions to specific individuals.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student data by teacher
description: The teacher (external entity) could share or disclose student submission data (names, work content, submission times) with unauthorized parties beyond the intended scope.

title: Manipulation of submission timestamps
description: Submission times displayed by the portal could be falsified or manipulated, potentially misleading the teacher about when work was actually submitted.

title: Teacher Identity Disclosure
description: Teacher's identity (grader id) is shared with the system, potentially revealing which teacher graded which student, enabling identification of the teacher's grading patterns and workload.

title: Student-Teacher Linkability
description: Data in transit contains student id and grader id, enabling linkage between students and their teachers, potentially revealing sensitive teacher-student relationships.

title: Unauthorized Grade Disclosure
description: Grades Portal Web App stores and processes student grades and feedback, potentially exposing sensitive academic information to unauthorized users or through inadequate access controls.

title: Grade Recording Non-Repudiation
description: Teacher may deny recording a specific grade or feedback, as the system relies on teacher's word without cryptographic proof of submission.

title: Grade Data Integrity Risk
description: System may not adequately validate or audit grade entries, allowing potential data corruption or manipulation of recorded grades.

title: Linkability of student identifiers in grade records
description: The grading service shares grade records containing student IDs, which could be used to link multiple records to the same student, potentially revealing patterns in grading or academic performance.

title: Direct identification of students via student IDs
description: Grade records contain explicit student identifiers, allowing direct identification of students from the database.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of grade records during transmission
description: Grade records transmitted from the grading service to the database could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transit.

title: Excessive data collection in grade records
description: Grade records may contain more data than necessary (e.g., detailed feedback) that could be minimized without affecting the grading process.

title: Unauthorized access to stored grade records
description: The grade records database may allow unauthorized access to sensitive student grade information.

title: Student shares identifying grade data
description: The student's request for grades involves sharing identifying information about themselves. Grades are inherently identifying data that can be linked to the student's identity.
assumptions: Grades are stored in a way that links them to student identity

title: System links grade request to other student data
description: The grades portal could link this grade request to other student records, potentially creating a comprehensive profile of the student across multiple data sources.
assumptions: The system has access to other student data that could be linked

title: Student identity could be usurped
description: An attacker could impersonate the student to access grades, potentially through credential theft, social engineering, or session hijacking.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be vulnerable to impersonation attacks

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student grades
description: The system might disclose grades to unauthorized parties, either through inadequate access controls, insider threats, or data breaches.
assumptions: Access controls may not be sufficiently restrictive

title: Data in transit could be intercepted and linked
description: Data transmitted between the student and the grades portal could be intercepted, potentially allowing an attacker to link the request to the student's identity.
assumptions: Data transmission may not be fully encrypted or protected

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student grades
description: The Grades Portal Web App may disclose student grades and teacher feedback to unauthorized parties through improper access controls or logging mechanisms.

title: Data interception during transmission
description: Grades and feedback data in transit between the portal and student could be intercepted by network attackers if not properly encrypted.

title: Metadata linkability of student data
description: Metadata about the data flow (e.g., timing, frequency, data volume) could be used to link or identify students based on their grade retrieval patterns.

title: Student identification through grade display
description: The act of displaying grades inherently identifies the student, potentially exposing sensitive academic information to unintended observers.

title: Student data usurpation
description: The student receiving grades could potentially use this information for identity-related purposes or share it with others, leading to unauthorized use of academic data.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child's grades to parent
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) shares sensitive academic information (grades, feedback, submission history) with the parent (EE2). If the portal lacks proper access controls or authentication, unauthorized parties could access this data during the sharing process.

title: Data interception during transmission
description: Data in transit from the portal to the parent could be intercepted by third parties. Without encryption, sensitive academic information could be exposed to unauthorized observers during transmission.

title: Parent misuse of child's academic data
description: The parent (EE2) may use the received academic information for purposes beyond the intended scope, such as sharing with third parties, using it for discrimination, or storing it insecurely.

title: Excessive data sharing with parent
description: The portal may share more detailed academic information than necessary for the parent to fulfill their role, violating data minimization principles.

title: Data Interception During Account Creation
description: Personal data (names, emails, roles, relationships) transmitted from administrator to web app could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission, enabling identification of parents and children.

title: Linkability of Parent-Child Relationships
description: Metadata about parent-child relationships in transit could be used to link this data with other datasets, potentially revealing family connections and enabling profiling.

title: Unauthorized Data Storage
description: The Grades Portal Web App may store sensitive parent-child relationship data without adequate access controls, risking unauthorized disclosure to internal or external parties.

title: Data Misuse for Unauthorized Purposes
description: The process may use stored parent-child relationship data for purposes beyond the intended scope (e.g., marketing, third-party sharing) without proper consent mechanisms.

title: False Account Information
description: Administrator may intentionally or unintentionally provide incorrect parent-child relationship data, leading to inaccurate records and potential privacy violations for affected families.

title: Data in transit exposed during account record transfer
description: Account records and parent-child relationship links transmitted from grading service to account directory may be intercepted or exposed during transit, potentially revealing sensitive student information to unauthorized parties.

title: Account directory improper access controls on stored records
description: The account directory may store account records and parent-child relationship links with insufficient access controls, allowing unauthorized access to sensitive student data.

title: Stored account data enables identification of students
description: The account directory stores account records containing personally identifiable information that can be used to identify individual students and their relationships.

title: Grading service shares data without proper consent
description: The assignment and grading service may write account records to the directory without obtaining or verifying proper consent from data subjects or their guardians.

title: Explicit Data Disclosure to Third-Party Cloud Provider
description: Full grade records, assignments, and account directory are intentionally transferred to external cloud hosting provider EE5. This represents explicit disclosure of personal data across organizational boundary, potentially violating minimality principle if all data elements are not strictly required for cloud hosting/backup purposes.
assumptions: Cloud provider EE5 has access to and processes this personal data for backup/replication purposes.

title: Linkability via Account Directory Data in Transit
description: Account directory data transferred in flow DF14 may contain identifiers enabling linking of students/users across systems. Metadata about data recipients and transfer patterns could be exploited to correlate identities across different contexts.
assumptions: Account directory contains personally identifiable information that can be used to link individuals.

title: Identification Risk During Data Transfer
description: Grade records and assignments transferred in transit may reveal individual student identities through content analysis or metadata. Third parties intercepting the flow could identify individuals based on unique assignment patterns or grade combinations.
assumptions: Data in transit is not adequately protected against interception or analysis.

title: Data Minimization Violation at Source
description: Process P2 shares full grade records, assignments, and account directory with EE5. Question whether all data elements are strictly necessary for cloud hosting/backup purposes, or if data minimization could reduce exposure by transferring only essential backup data.
assumptions: Not all transferred data elements are required for the stated purpose of cloud hosting and backup.
